raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation On the per-rank fused shared-slot path, `_post_process_topk_ids` ends with a `_zero_topk_weights_padded_region` launch, once per MoE layer, that exists only to undo what the append kernel left behind. `_fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep_kernel` already takes `num_token_non_padded`, but its `HAS_PADDING` branch only fills the routed **ids** for padded rows — it stores the gate's weights untouched, and writes the shared slots unconditionally at `scale_factor`. So a padded row leaves the append with live weights, and a second full pass over `topk_weights` is needed to zero them. ## Modification Zero them in the append instead, on both the routed and the shared tile. The row is already in registers there, so it costs a `tl.where` on each tile, and a padded row now leaves that kernel fully inert. The trailing pass is then redundant whenever the fold was active, so it is skipped in that case. It still runs otherwise, which is required: the append only receives `num_token_non_padded` when the fold is active, so `HAS_PADDING` is false on every other path and those rows are still zeroed by the trailing pass exactly as before. 16 lines across two files. ## Effect Traces Before Traces After One kernel launch per MoE layer disappears, along with a read and a write of `topk_weights` that the preceding kernel does for free. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI with `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`. Rank-0 device kernel time over a profiled window of 5 decode steps; both arms are the same image and differ only by this commit: | kernel | base calls | base us | patch calls | patch us | | ------ | ---------: | ------: | ----------: | ------: | | `_fused_append_remap_shared_experts_deepep_kernel` | 290 | 1388.9 | 290 | 1256.4 | | `_fill_padded_rows_kernel` | 320 | 1348.2 | 30 | 96.3 | | total | 610 | 2737.1 | 320 | 1352.7 | The pad-fill count drops by exactly 290, the same as the append count, which is the fold engaging one-for-one. That is 58 fewer launches and ~250 us per decode step. The 30 remaining calls are the paths where the fold does not apply, and they are unchanged. **This is not a throughput change, and should not be read as one.** The whole MoE routing stage is ~1% of device kernel time in this configuration, so a saving of this size is well inside run-to-run noise: | metric | base | patch | | ------ | ---- | ----- | | output throughput | 293.97 tok/s | 295.89 tok/s | | total throughput | 4997.57 tok/s | 5030.15 tok/s | | mean TPOT | 115.75 ms | 115.66 ms | It removes redundant work, not a bottleneck. ## Accuracy The risk here is a padded row escaping with a live weight, which is wrong output rather than an error, so accuracy is the check that matters. GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319: | arm | accuracy | invalid | | --- | -------- | ------- | | base | 0.948 | 0.000 | | patch | 0.951 | 0.000 | The gap is four questions out of 1319, which is inside run-to-run noise for this benchmark; the point is that the padded rows stayed inert, not that the change improves accuracy.
Commands ``` SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \ SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1 \ SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 \ GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=8G \ MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \ --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal \ --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-dp-lm-head \ --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \ --context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \ --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 # Trace python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 64 \ --profile --profile-steps 6 --profile-output-dir $OUT # Accuracy python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 ```
Note: both arms are branched from `main` without #36515, so they carry the shared-slot double-append bug identically; it cancels out of this comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Kernel trace shows the launch removed, one-for-one with the append - [x] Accuracy measured on MI355X, 1319 questions, one arm per side - [x] Each arm asserted which side of the change it was on before measuring - [x] Trailing pass still runs on paths where the fold is inactive - [x] No new configuration --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #38978994871](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38978994871) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #38978991399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38978991399) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #38978991009](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38978991009)
